body:
The completed source refresh confirms the unsupported whole-material chemistry; the shared-owner identity remains unresolved. The Step 7d assessment has stopped before the required full review because the coordinator verified a separate workflow stop condition. No source or mapping changes have been applied, and this issue remains open.

At main `467aa319a06ef992035f509f66fe251082b44ae1`, `Glycerol_Phosphate_Disodium_Salt_Hydrate.yaml` still has SHA256 `34a148f0b60690558fc0aa0970a93b619fd340e057a3e07e490000b94d3859bc`. On 2026-11-03 UTC, successful primary GET responses reproduced the previously inspected bytes:

- [Sigma-Aldrich's PubChem SID24895257](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/substance/sid/24895257/JSON), version 6, source `G6501_SIGMA`, names an isomeric mixture; SHA256 `229b66301e98e2ea1a4b8fc032121244c80376c398a9d31e45759c0be917937a`.
- [GSRS RCS9EQ01V4](https://gsrs.ncats.nih.gov/api/v1/substances/RCS9EQ01V4?view=full) classifies CAS 55073-41-1 as a mixture and lists sodium 2-glycerophosphate pentahydrate and sodium 1-glycerophosphate hexahydrate as required components; SHA256 `930bfa931206f64225a94fa9aaeee12240f217f918b3f59551fb5dc531b2ff33`.
- [NCIT:C120561](https://api-evsrest.nci.nih.gov/api/v1/concept/ncit/C120561?include=full) retains the same CAS/UNII and disodium-hydrate synonym; SHA256 `8f36309df9aae2aa5f10857cffce7184c0fb0632f536761fa8f619b7c44dd5e8`.

These sources do not support the record's single water-free positional formula/InChI/SMILES as exact chemistry of the whole supplied material. Removing that unsupported active chemistry can be scoped without merging owners. A future guarded correction should preserve the prior values and history, retain the sourced catalogue context, and avoid replacing them with an averaged formula, guessed water count or inferred component proportions. The supplier-deposited record is distinct from the earlier failed supplier-HTML request; that failure remains failed evidence.

This does not settle assignment to the existing `Sodium_glycerophosphate` owner, whose current identifier is NCIT:C120561 and whose source context is CultureMech. Shared registry/ontology metadata does not determine whether those source occurrences and the G6501 catalogue material should share one record. No identity reassignment, occurrence transfer, inherited support or merge is justified by this partial assessment.

Recommendation: drop G6501 from the proposed #901 identity/predicate migration until its source boundary is resolved, keeping its existing holds and provisional role. The narrower chemistry cleanup may be considered separately when authorized execution resumes; it would not by itself close this issue's ownership question. This interrupted assessment is not a completed native per-owner review, a new mapping approval or a resolution of #1118. Evidence and GET receipts are retained under `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/step7d-execution-20261103/priority-science/`.

The completed current-byte review confirms the chemistry defect but leaves the source-owner boundary unresolved. **Drop the entire `Glycerol_Phosphate_Disodium_Salt_Hydrate` owner from Step 7d, including partial chemistry cleanup, and leave this issue open.** No record or mapping has changed.

The original catalogue selects Sigma G6501 / CAS 55073-41-1. [Sigma's deposited PubChem SID 24895257](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/substance/sid/24895257/JSON) describes an isomeric mixture. [GSRS RCS9EQ01V4](https://gsrs.ncats.nih.gov/api/v1/substances/RCS9EQ01V4?view=full) classifies it as a mixture and lists the 1- and 2-glycerophosphate hydrate components; it links [NCIT:C120561](https://api-evsrest.nci.nih.gov/api/v1/concept/ncit/C120561?include=full). The active single-isomer, water-free formula/InChI/SMILES/CID do not describe that whole supplied material. No averaged formula, fixed water count or component proportion follows from these sources.

The neighboring `Sodium_glycerophosphate` record already owns NCIT:C120561 and has a different CultureMech source context. Shared registry links do not resolve whether its source occurrences and catalogue G6501 should share an owner. Options are to preserve separate source-form records with explicit distinctions, or to consolidate only after a source-by-source equivalence and occurrence audit. Recommendation: retain the distinct records and current holds while that audit is pending; later withdraw or properly scope the unsupported whole-mixture chemistry through a guarded correction. Step 7d will neither merge them nor transfer occurrences or support.

The reviewed G6501 bytes remain SHA256 `34a148f0b60690558fc0aa0970a93b619fd340e057a3e07e490000b94d3859bc` at main `467aa319a06ef992035f509f66fe251082b44ae1`. Individual and aggregate records agree; native strict and term checks pass. Those structural results do not settle the scientific boundary. The full review and precise evidence captures are in `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/step7d-execution-20261103/science-b/full-assessments.json`, SHA256 `faab3185341abeef1e3b79a16593ab408c468c8164c49e8e81d8ab0c4bd6c2ef`.

The owner will be listed as dropped in #901 and the Step 7d PR. Its provisional roles, existing mapping holds and the separate #1053 and #1020 work remain unchanged. This conclusion grants no new scientific approval.
